extracted.intended_audience: Principal Investigators who have an ERC frontier research main grant and are considering/applying for an ERC Proof of Concept (PoC) Grant
extracted.subtask_short: ERC Proof of Concept grant application
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluation criteria for preparing and submitting an ERC Proof of Concept (PoC) grant application to explore the commercial or societal potential of ideas arising from an ERC-funded frontier research project.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility — ERC award and relation to ERC-funded research
rubrics_metrics.description: The ERC Proof of Concept funding is made available only to those who already have an ERC award to establish proof of concept of an idea that was generated in the course of their ERC-funded projects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Principal Investigators in one of the ERC frontier research main grants (Starting, Consolidator, Advanced or Synergy) are eligible. The Principal Investigator must be able to demonstrate the relation between the idea to be taken to proof of concept and the ERC frontier research project in question. Proposals must draw substantially on the ERC funded research.

rubrics_metrics.name: PI timing eligibility (ongoing or recently ended grants)
rubrics_metrics.description: Principal Investigators in an ongoing main grant, or Principal Investigators in a main grant that has ended after 1 January 2025, are eligible to apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This temporal condition determines which former PIs may still apply; verify grant end date against the 1 January 2025 cutoff.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission limits and Synergy-specific restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: A Principal Investigator may submit only one application per call. A maximum of three Proof of Concept Grants may be awarded per main grant project, except for Synergy Grant where a maximum of six may be awarded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Synergy Grant Principal Investigators are eligible to apply only with the written consent of all Principal Investigators in the same Synergy Grant project.

rubrics_metrics.name: Host Institution (HI) eligibility and engagement requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The Host Institution must engage the Principal Investigator for at least the duration of the Proof of Concept project and must be established in an EU Member State or associated country, or be an International European Interest Organisation, the JRC, or any other entity created under EU law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any type of legal entity, public or private (including universities, research organisations and undertakings), can host PIs. Private for-profit research centres, including industrial laboratories, are welcome. International organisations with headquarters in an EU Member State/AC are deemed established there. The PI may submit with a different HI than their main grant provided the HI complies with eligibility criteria in the Work Programme.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grant funding model, amount and duration
rubrics_metrics.description: Proof of Concept Grants are awarded as a lump sum of EUR 150,000 for a period of 18 months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Work Programme 2026 continues this lump-sum model. Applicants must plan activities to fit the fixed budget and time (18 months).

rubrics_metrics.name: Required application components and submission rules
rubrics_metrics.description: A complete application needs to include the administrative form, the proposal (Part B) and the supplementary documents (Host Institution binding statement of support and if applicable ethics self-assessment, additional ethics documentation and letters of support or intent).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications can be submitted from the opening date of the chosen call until the specified submission deadline. Calls are published on this page, the EU Funding & Tenders Portal and in the Official Journal of the EU. Ensure all required documents are provided by the chosen call deadline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose and scope of eligible Proof of Concept proposals
rubrics_metrics.description: Proof of Concept funding is intended to establish proof of concept of an idea generated in the course of an ERC-funded project by funding further work (activities not scheduled to be funded by the original ERC frontier research grant) to verify innovation potential.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The objective is to enable ERC-funded ideas to progress from ground‑breaking research towards innovation. Proposals must draw substantially on ERC-funded research and aim to maximise the value of the ERC-funded research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of activities appropriate for PoC proposals
rubrics_metrics.description: Activities funded should facilitate exploration of the commercial and social innovation potential, such as testing, experimenting, demonstrating and validating the idea; conducting research required to carry out these activities and address uncovered weaknesses; establishing viability and technical issues; clarifying IPR/knowledge transfer strategy; involving partners and stakeholders; assessing potential end users.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these activity types as a checklist when designing the proposal. Demonstrate how the planned activities will verify innovation potential and move the idea toward innovation or market/social uptake.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethics review requirement and basis
rubrics_metrics.description: Each proposal selected for funding must undergo an ethics review, a legal requirement under the Horizon Europe Framework Programme (Regulation 2021/695: Articles 18–19). The basis for ethics review is Part A (including the Ethics Issues Table and Ethics Self-Assessment) and Part B of the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A well-detailed Ethics Self-Assessment (ESA) is crucial; it clarifies issues linked to proposed research activities and how they will be dealt with. Research involving hESCs requires all ethics steps and a specific EC approval via comitology.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethics review process and stages
rubrics_metrics.description: The ethics review comprises three stages: Ethics pre-screening (internally by ERCEA), Ethics screening (panels of independent ethics reviewers) and Ethics assessment (panels of independent ethics reviewers discussing serious/complex issues).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pre-screening clears proposals without ethics issues or with simple issues. Screening identifies potentially Serious and/or Complex issues; clearance of non-Serious/Complex issues may include observations and requests for documents to be kept on file. Applicants may be contacted for additional information (typically one week after the screening panel) and are given 3 weeks to reply. If follow-up during implementation is needed, ethics deliverables might be formulated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation principle — sole criterion of excellence
rubrics_metrics.description: The Proof of Concept Grant is evaluated based on the sole criterion of excellence, which comprises three evaluation elements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only excellence is assessed; the three elements together define excellence for PoC proposals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation element — Breakthrough innovation potential
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals will have to demonstrate that the proposed Proof of Concept activity has the potential to drive innovation and business inventiveness and/or tackle societal challenges, and that the proposed expected outcomes are innovative or distinctive compared to existing solutions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show how outcomes would be innovative/distinctive vs existing solutions and how the activity could drive innovation or societal impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation element — Approach and methodology
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposed Proof of Concept activities and planning are feasible within the proposed timescales and resources, and are appropriate and effective to explore the pathway from ground‑breaking research towards innovation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrate feasibility, realistic planning, and that methods are appropriate and effective for exploring the path from research to innovation. Include timelines, resource allocation and risk/contingency measures where relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation element — Principal Investigator: strategic lead and project management
rubrics_metrics.description: The Principal Investigator needs to demonstrate a clear vision on how to organise the management of the project, the consolidation of information and data needed to take strategic decisions and implement the proposed plan, including risk and contingency measures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasise PI's strategic leadership, management structures, decision‑making processes, data consolidation plans, and risk/contingency planning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scoring labels and pass requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: External independent experts will mark each of the three evaluation elements as 'very good', 'good' or 'fail'. To be considered for funding, proposals must be awarded a pass mark ('very good' or 'good') by a majority of the experts on each of the three evaluation elements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A majority pass on each element is required (i.e., not overall average) — applicants must aim to meet all three elements to be fundable. The process is single-stage submission and single-step evaluation (two cut-off dates as of 2024).

rubrics_metrics.name: Seal of Excellence recognition and follow-up options
rubrics_metrics.description: A Seal of Excellence will be awarded to proposals that have received a pass mark in all three evaluation elements but cannot be funded due to lack of budget.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants awarded a Seal of Excellence can consult lists of national and regional support programmes for Seal holders or contact National Contact Points and their host country to enquire about funding opportunities.
